body:
I'm not familiar with how to actually implement `stable_sort`, but it looks like the logic ends up doing something like this:
```cpp
    std::vector<std::string> stuff = {"a", "b", "c"};
    auto cpy = stuff; // this is our temporary buffer

    auto first = stuff.begin();
    auto middle = stuff.begin() + 1;
    auto last = stuff.end();

    ranges::merge(
        ranges::make_move_iterator(cpy.begin()),
        ranges::make_move_iterator(cpy.begin() + 1),
        ranges::make_move_iterator(middle),
        ranges::make_move_iterator(last),
        first,
        ranges::less(),
        ranges::identity(),
        ranges::identity());


    fmt::print("{}\n", stuff); // ["a", "", ""]
```

Which in this specific case is basically self-move-assigning all the elements after the first. Which is why those get wiped. 

I wonder if the issue is `merge_adaptive` calling `merge` on overlapping ranges.
